item.title: Continental Grid Pact Clears Final Hurdle as Member States Lock In Cross-Border Transmission
item.description:
BRUSSELS — After nineteen months of closed-door drafting sessions and three stalled ministerial summits, lawmakers finalized a binding continental grid accord late Tuesday that compels national transmission operators to allocate at least 70 percent of interconnector capacity to cross-border electricity flows.

The legislation targets a persistent structural bottleneck: clean generation in coastal wind corridors routinely gets curtailed while inland manufacturing hubs burn natural gas reserves only a few hundred kilometers away.
